stores</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company generates revenue from retail sales where control is transferred and revenue is recognized at the point of sale. &#160;Retail sales are recorded net of estimated returns and exclude sales tax. &#160;The Company records&#160;a returns reserve and a corresponding return asset for expected returns of merchandise.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Retail sales to members of the Company&#8217;s loyalty programs, including the Famously You Rewards program, include <ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_item_gZmsljvwcUOp7uEbOPNoGQ" contextRef="Duration_2_4_2024_To_11_2_2024_84r8zrosWkeyG_pcft4uEg" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" name="cal:NumberOfPerformanceObligations" scale="0" id="Narr_9n6K8xuj00qsRsmtO7W6qQ">two</ix:nonFraction> performance obligations: the sale of merchandise and the delivery of points that may be converted to savings certificates and redeemed for future purchases. &#160;The transaction price is allocated to the separate performance obligations based on the relative stand-alone selling price. &#160;The stand-alone selling price for the points is estimated using the retail value of the merchandise earned, adjusted for estimated breakage based upon historical redemption patterns. &#160;The revenue associated with the initial merchandise purchased is recognized immediately and the value assigned to the points is deferred until the points are redeemed, forfeited or expired.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">E-commerce</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company generates revenue from sales on websites maintained by the Company that are shipped from the Company&#8217;s distribution centers or retail stores directly to the consumer, or picked up directly by the consumer from the Company&#8217;s stores (&#8220;e-commerce &#8211; Company websites&#8221;); sales from the Company&#8217;s wholesale customers&#8217; websites that are fulfilled on a drop-ship basis (&#8220;e-commerce &#8211; wholesale drop ship&#8221;); and other e-commerce sales (&#8220;wholesale &#8211; e-commerce&#8221;), collectively referred to as "e-commerce". &#160;The Company transfers control and recognizes revenue for merchandise sold that is shipped directly to an individual consumer upon delivery to the consumer.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Landed wholesale</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Landed sales are wholesale sales in which the Company obtains title to the footwear from the overseas suppliers and maintains title until the merchandise is shipped to the customer from the Company&#8217;s warehouses. &#160;Many customers purchasing footwear on a landed basis arrange their own transportation of merchandise and, with limited exceptions, control is transferred at the time of shipment. &#160;Landed sales generally carry a higher profit rate than first-cost wholesale sales as a result of the brand equity associated with the product along with the additional customs, warehousing and logistics services provided to customers and the risks associated with inventory ownership.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">First-cost wholesale</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">First-cost sales are wholesale sales in which the Company purchases merchandise from an international factory that manufactures the product and subsequently sells to a customer at an overseas port. Many of the customers then import this product into the United States. &#160;Revenue is recognized at the time the merchandise is delivered to the customer&#8217;s designated freight forwarder and control is transferred to the customer.</p></ix:continuation></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">11</p></div></div>

Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Licensing and royalty</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company has license agreements with third parties allowing them to sell the Company&#8217;s branded product, or other merchandise that uses the Company&#8217;s owned or licensed brand names. These license agreements provide the licensee access to the Company&#8217;s symbolic intellectual property, and revenue is therefore recognized over the license term. For royalty contracts that do not have guaranteed minimums, the Company recognizes revenue as the licensee&#8217;s sales occur. For royalty contracts that have guaranteed minimums, revenue for the guaranteed minimum is recognized on a straight-line basis during the term, until such time that the cumulative royalties exceed the total minimum guarantee. Up-front payments are recognized over the contractual term to which the guaranteed minimum relates.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company also licenses its Famous Footwear trade name and logo to a third-party financial institution to offer Famous Footwear-branded credit cards to its consumers. &#160;The Company receives royalties based upon cardholder spending, which is recognized as licensing revenue at the time the credit card is used. &#160; &#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Contract Balances</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Revenue is recorded at the transaction price, net of estimates for variable consideration for which reserves are established, including returns, allowances and discounts. Variable consideration is estimated using the expected value method and given the large number of contracts with similar characteristics, the portfolio approach is applied to determine the variable consideration for each revenue stream. Reserves for projected returns are based on historical patterns and current expectations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New stock at no cost to the non-employee director. &#160;The RSUs are subject to a vesting requirement (usually one year) and earn dividend equivalents at the same rate as dividends on the Company&#8217;s common stock. &#160;The dividend equivalents, which vest immediately, are automatically reinvested in additional RSUs. &#160;Expense related to the initial grant of RSUs is recognized ratably over the vesting period based upon the fair value of the RSUs. &#160;The RSUs payable in cash are remeasured at the end of each period. &#160;Expense for the dividend equivalents is recognized at fair value when the dividend equivalents are granted. &#160;Gains and losses resulting from changes in the fair value of the RSUs payable in cash subsequent to the vesting period and through the settlement date of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs to the extent possible. &#160;The Company also considers counterparty credit risk in its assessment of fair value. &#160;Classification of the financial or non-financial asset or liability within the hierarchy is determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Measurement of Fair Value</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company measures fair value as an exit price, the price to sell an asset or transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, using the procedures described below for all financial and non-financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Non-Qualified Deferred Compensation Plan Assets and Liabilities</p><p style="font-family:'Times New the benefit of certain management employees. &#160;The investment funds offered to the participants generally correspond to the funds offered in the Company&#8217;s 401(k)&#160;plan, and the account balance fluctuates with the investment returns on those funds. &#160;The Deferred Compensation Plan permits the deferral of up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_pure_wSfnaJauBUuZVBMqXwM0Mw" Plan&#8221;) for the benefit of certain members of executive management. &#160;The Restoration Plan provides an incremental retirement benefit to key executives whose contributions to qualified retirement plans are limited by Internal Revenue Service annual compensation maximums. &#160;The investment funds offered to the participants generally correspond to the funds offered in the Company&#8217;s 401(k)&#160;plan. &#160;The initial contribution to the Restoration Plan was funded in January 2024 and contributions are expected to continue on an annual basis. The plan assets and liabilities will fluctuate with the returns on the investment funds. &#160;The deferrals are held in a separate trust, which has been established by the Company to administer the Restoration Plan. &#160;The assets of the trust are subject to the claims of the Company&#8217;s creditors in the event that the Company becomes insolvent. &#160;Consequently, the trust qualifies as a grantor trust for income tax purposes (i.e., a &#8220;Rabbi Trust&#8221;). &#160;The liabilities of the Restoration Plan are presented in other accrued expenses and the assets held by the trust are classified within prepaid and other current assets in the condensed consolidated balance sheets. &#160; style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Environmental Remediation</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Prior operations included numerous manufacturing and other facilities for which the Company may have responsibility under various environmental laws for the remediation of conditions that may be identified in the future. &#160;The Company is involved in environmental remediation and ongoing compliance activities at several sites and has been notified that it is or may be a potentially responsible party at several other sites.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Redfield</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company is remediating, under the oversight of Colorado authorities, the groundwater and indoor air at its owned facility in Colorado (the &#8220;Redfield site&#8221; or, when referring to remediation activities at or under the facility, the &#8220;on-site remediation&#8221;) and residential neighborhoods adjacent to and near the property (the &#8220;off-site remediation&#8221;) that have been affected by solvents previously used at the facility. &#160;The on-site remediation calls for the operation of a pump and treat system (which prevents migration of contaminated groundwater off the property) as the final remedy for the site, subject to monitoring and periodic review of the on-site conditions and other remedial technologies that may be developed in the future. &#160;In 2016, the Company submitted a revised plan to address on-site conditions, including direct treatment of source areas, and received approval from the oversight authorities to begin implementing the revised plan. &#160;The Company received permission from the oversight authorities to convert the pump and treat system to a passive treatment barrier system and completed the conversion during 2023.</p></ix:nonNumeric></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">24</p></div></div>

In accordance with the work plan, a pilot test was conducted of certain groundwater remediation methods and the results of that test were used to develop more detailed plans for remedial activities in the off-site areas, which were approved by the authorities and are being implemented in a phased manner. &#160;The results of groundwater monitoring are being used to evaluate the effectiveness of these activities. &#160;The Company continues to implement the expanded remedy work plan that was approved by the oversight authorities in 2015 and to work with the oversight authorities on the off-site work plan.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The cumulative expenditures for both on-site and off-site ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><a id="_Hlk72503510"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;padding-bottom:1pt;border-bottom:1.0pt solid #000000;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">OVERVIEW</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Business Overview</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">We are a global footwear company that operates retail stores and e-commerce websites, and designs, develops, sources, manufactures and distributes footwear for people of all ages. &#160;Our mission is to inspire people to feel great...feet first. &#160;We offer retailers and consumers a diversified portfolio of leading footwear brands. &#160;Outfitted in our brands, customers can step confidently into every aspect of their lives. &#160;As both a retailer and a wholesaler, we have a perspective on the marketplace that enables us to serve consumers from different vantage points. &#160;We believe our diversified business model provides us with synergies by spanning consumer segments, categories and distribution channels. &#160;A combination of thoughtful planning and rigorous execution is key to our success in optimizing our business and portfolio of brands. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Known Trends Impacting Our Business</b></p><a id="_Hlk136603637"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Based on the current macroeconomic environment and our recent operating results, we believe the following trends may continue to impact our business and operating results:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Macroeconomic Environment </i><b style="color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold;"> </b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Macroeconomic factors, including, among others, inflation, elevated interest rates, increased real estate costs and higher consumer debt levels continued to impact consumer discretionary spending and our financial results during the first nine months of 2024. &#160;We continued to experience lighter consumer traffic in our retail stores during the third quarter, resulting in lower net sales. &#160;While we believe that the structural changes we have implemented in the last few years, as well as our diversified model and operational discipline, enable the Company to drive value in a variety of market conditions, changes in macro-level consumer spending trends may continue to adversely impact our financial results in the future. &#160;We believe our focus on cost control and our commitment to execute our clearly defined strategic initiatives have positioned us for sustainable, long-term growth.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Liquidity </i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Our liquidity position remains strong, with $33.4 million in cash and cash equivalents and excess availability on our revolving credit agreement of $252.1 million as of November 2, 2024. &#160;During the nine months ended November 2, 2024, borrowings on our revolving credit agreement increased by $53.8 million to $238.5 million, primarily driven by $65.5 million of our common stock repurchases under our share repurchase programs. &#160;While our interest expense during the fourth quarter of 2024 will continue to be negatively impacted by the elevated interest rates, we expect to reduce the borrowings under our revolving credit agreement to mitigate the impact of the high interest rate environment. &#160; <div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:91.06%;border:0;margin:30pt 4.47% 30pt 4.47%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:4.47%;padding-right:4.47%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a style="color:#000000;font-family:&quot;'Times New Roman','Times','serif'&quot;;font-size:10pt;" href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-left:-10.0pt;margin-right:-10.0pt;max-width:100%;position:relative;width:calc(100% + 20.0pt);"><div style="padding-left:10pt;padding-right:10pt;position:relative;width:100%;"><a id="_Hlk135909861"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Metrics Used in the Evaluation of Our Business</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The following are&#160;a few key metrics by which we evaluate our business, identify trends&#160;and make strategic decisions:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Comparable sales</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The comparable sales metric is a metric commonly used in the retail industry to evaluate the revenue generated for stores that have been open for more than a&#160;year, though other&#160;retailers may calculate the metric differently. &#160;Management uses the comparable sales metric as a measure of an individual store&#8217;s success to determine whether it is performing in line with expectations. &#160;Our comparable sales metric is a daily-weighted calculation for the period, which includes sales for stores that have been open for at least 13&#160;months. &#160;In addition, in order to be included in the comparable sales metric, a store must be open in the current period as well as the corresponding day(s)&#160;of the comparable retail calendar in the prior&#160;year. &#160;Accordingly, closed stores are excluded from the comparable sales metric for each day of the closure. &#160;Relocated stores are treated as new stores and therefore excluded from the calculation. &#160;E-commerce sales for those websites that function as an extension of a retail chain are included in the comparable sales calculation. &#160;In fiscal years with 53 weeks (e.g. 2023), the 53<sup style="font-size:7.5pt;line-height:100%;top:0pt;vertical-align:top;">rd</sup> week of comparable sales is included in the calculation. &#160;In the following year (e.g. 2024), the prior fiscal year period is shifted by one week to compare similar calendar weeks. &#160;We believe the comparable sales metric is useful to shareholders and investors in assessing our retail sales performance of existing locations with comparable prior&#160;year sales, separate from the impact of store openings or store closures.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt;">Sales per square foot</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The sales per square foot metric is commonly used in the retail industry to<i style="font-style:italic;">&#160;</i>calculate the efficiency of sales based upon the square footage in a store. &#160;Management uses the sales per square foot metric as a measure of an individual store&#8217;s success to determine whether it is performing in line with expectations. The sales per square foot metric is calculated by dividing total retail store sales, excluding e-commerce sales and the retail operations of our joint venture in China, by the total square footage of the retail store base in North America at the end of each&#160;month of the respective period. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Dire</i><i style="font-style:italic;">ct-to-consumer sales</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Direct-to-consumer sales includes sales from our retail stores, our company-owned websites and sales through our customers&#8217; websites that we fulfill on a drop-ship basis. &#160;While we take an omni-channel approach to reach consumers, we believe that our direct-to-consumer channels reinforce the image of our brands and strengthens our connection with the end consumer. &#160;In addition, direct-to-consumer sales generally result in a higher gross margin for the Company as compared to wholesale sales. &#160;As a result, management monitors trends in direct-to-consumer sales as a percentage of our Brand Portfolio segment and total consolidated net sales.</p><a id="_Hlk183106412"></a><a id="_41e5c041_2e35_41c1_8c71_961381ee037f"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;padding-bottom:1pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;margin:0pt;">RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Following are the consolidated results and the results by segment:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span Sales</p><a id="_Hlk175130824"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Net sales decreased $21.0 million, or 2.8%, to $740.9&#160;million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$761.9 million for the third quarter of 2023, driven by a $21.5 million, or 4.8%, decline in net sales for our Famous Footwear segment largely due to the retail calendar shift associated with the 53<sup style="font-size:7.5pt;line-height:100%;top:0pt;vertical-align:top;">rd</sup> week in fiscal year 2023, as well as softer seasonal demand in the boots category. &#160;The decrease in the Famous </p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New segment net sales was partially offset by an increase in net sales in the Brand Portfolio segment of $2.2 million, or 0.7% during the third quarter of 2024, with our brands with premium positioning generally outperforming our other brands. &#160;We also experienced growth in sales from our owned e-commerce businesses, which increased approximately 2.1% on a consolidated basis compared to the third quarter of 2023. &#160;Our direct-to-consumer sales represented approximately 72% of consolidated net sales for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 73% in the third quarter of 2023. &#160;We remain focused on maximizing the vertical opportunity between the Famous Footwear and Brand Portfolio segments, with LifeStride, Dr. Scholl&#8217;s, Naturalizer and Blowfish Malibu representing four of Famous Footwear&#8217;s top 20 best-selling footwear brands during the quarter.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Net sales decreased $36.7 million, or 1.7%, to $2,083.5 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $2,120.2 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;Net sales for our Brand Portfolio segment decreased $21.6 million, or 2.3% during the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;In addition, net sales for our Famous Footwear segment decreased $15.1 million, or 1.2%, in the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to the nine months ended October 28, 2023, due in part to a decline in customer traffic in our retail stores. &#160;Comparable sales decreased 0.9% in the nine months ended November 2, 2024. &#160;On a consolidated basis, our direct-to-consumer sales were approximately 72% of total net sales for both the nine months ended November 2, 2024 and the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Gross Profit</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Gross profit decreased $13.4&#160;million, or 3.9%,&#160;to $327.0 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to $340.4 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, gross profit decreased to&#160;44.1% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;44.7% for the third quarter of 2023, driven by a decrease in the gross margin of our Famous Footwear segment, partially offset by a slight increase in the gross margin of our Brand Portfolio segment. &#160;The lower gross margin at Famous Footwear reflects an increase in promotional activity and higher clearance sales, partially due to aged boot inventory. &#160;In addition, we experienced higher freight costs, due in part to the higher mix of e-commerce sales.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Gross profit decreased $10.3 million, or 1.1%, to $946.9 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $957.2 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;As a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 45.5% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 45.1% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023, driven by an increase in the gross margin of our Brand Portfolio segment, reflecting higher merchandise margins and a higher mix of retail sales, including e-commerce sales from our owned brands and sales from our branded retail stores, both of which have higher gross margins than our wholesale sales. &#160;This increase was partially offset by a decrease in the gross margin in the Famous Footwear segment, driven by higher levels of promotional activity and clearance sales.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We classify certain warehousing, distribution, sourcing and other inventory procurement costs in selling and administrative expenses. &#160;Accordingly, our gross profit and selling and administrative expense rates, as a&#160;percentage of net sales, may not be comparable to other companies.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Selling and Administrative Expenses</p><a id="_Hlk58308664"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses decreased $5.0 million, or 1.8%, to&#160;$268.7 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$273.7 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;The decrease was driven by lower expenses for our cash and share-based incentive compensation. &#160;The decrease was partially offset by higher facilities costs, reflecting higher depreciation associated with the investment in Famous Footwear store renovations and upgrades and higher store rent expense as leases are renewed, higher salary and benefit expenses, higher information technology and consulting expense associated with the implementation of our cloud-based ERP platform, and higher marketing expenses driven by marketing investments for certain brands. As a&#160;percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased to 36.2%&#160;for the third quarter of 2024, from&#160;35.9% for the third quarter of 2023.<span style="background:#ffff00;"> </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses increased $13.7 million, or 1.7%, to&#160;$803.3 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$789.6 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The increase was primarily due to higher salary and benefit expenses, higher marketing expenses, higher information technology and consulting expense associated with the implementation of our cloud-based ERP platform, and higher facilities costs, partially offset by lower expenses for our cash and share-based incentive compensation. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased to 38.6%&#160;for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, from&#160;37.2% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">28</p></div></div>

to&#160;$2.9 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$4.5 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;Interest expense, net decreased&#160;$5.3 million, or 34.2%, to&#160;$10.0 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$15.3 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The decreases primarily reflect lower average borrowings on the revolving credit facility. &#160;The interest on our revolving credit facility is based on a variable rate, which adversely impacts our interest expense in the current elevated interest rate environment. &#160;While our interest expense for the remainder of 2024 will continue to be adversely impacted by the elevated interest rates, we expect to reduce the borrowings under our revolving credit agreement to mitigate the impact of the high interest rate environment. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Other Income, Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Our effective tax rate can vary considerably from period to period, depending on a number of factors. &#160;Our consolidated effective tax rate was 23.6% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 23.5% for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;Our consolidated effective tax rate was 23.8% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 24.1% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The lower effective tax rate was driven by discrete tax benefits, primarily related to share-based compensation, of approximately $1.1 million in the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $0.9 million in the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;line-height:1.27;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In 2021, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) released Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion model rules, designed to ensure large corporations are taxed at a minimum rate of 15% in all countries of operation. &#160;The OECD continues to release guidance and countries are implementing legislation to adopt the rules, which became effective on January 1, 2024. &#160;The United States has not yet enacted legislation implementing Pillar Two. &#160;We are continuing to evaluate the Pillar Two rules and their potential impact on future periods, but we do not expect the rules to have a material impact on our tax provision or effective tax rate.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Net Earnings&#160;Attributable to Caleres,&#160;Inc.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Net earnings attributable to Caleres,&#160;Inc. were $41.4&#160;million and $102.3 million for the third quarter and nine months ended November 2, 2024, respectively, compared to $46.9 million and $115.6 million for the third quarter and nine months ended October 28, 2023, respectively, as a result of the factors described above.</p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span id="_Hlk183105626"></a><a id="_Hlk144372019"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Net sales of $428.3 million in the third quarter of 2024 decreased $21.5&#160;million, or 4.8%, compared to the third quarter of 2023 driven by the retail calendar shift associated with the 53<sup style="font-size:7.5pt;line-height:100%;top:0pt;vertical-align:top;">rd</sup> week in fiscal year 2023. &#160;The shift resulted in one less week of our high-volume back-to-school selling season in the third quarter of 2024 compared to the third quarter of last year. &#160;Comparable sales, which reflects the calendar shift, increased 2.5%. &#160;We experienced a strong start to the third quarter of 2024 with the back-to-school selling season, but sales moderated as the quarter progressed. &#160;During the third quarter of 2024, we experienced soft demand in our boots category due in part to the unseasonably warm fall weather. &#160;Our sales were also adversely impacted by late product receipts of certain athletic footwear during the important back-to-school selling season. &#160;Our kids category, which is a key differentiator for Famous Footwear, continues to outperform many of our categories. &#160;Penetration of the kids category to total Famous Footwear sales was 25% in the third quarter of 2024. &#160;Our athletics category performed well during the quarter, driven by several of our key brands. &#160;We also experienced growth in our e-commerce sales and higher penetration of this channel in the third quarter of 2024. &#160;Penetration of e-commerce sales increased to approximately 15% of net sales in the third quarter of 2024, compared to 13% in the third quarter of 2023. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We opened six stores and closed 10 stores during the third quarter of 2024, resulting in 851 stores and total square footage of 5.6&#160;million at the end of the&#160;quarter, compared to 862 stores and total square footage of 5.7 million at the end of the&#160;third quarter of 2023. &#160;Sales to members of our customer loyalty program, Famously You Rewards, continue to account for a majority of the segment&#8217;s sales, with approximately 74% of our net sales made to program members in the third quarter of 2024, compared to 77% in the third quarter of 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Net sales of $1,198.1 million in the nine months ended November 2, 2024 decreased $15.1&#160;million, or 1.2%, compared to the nine months ended October 28, 2023, primarily due to the same factors described for the third quarter. &#160;Comparable sales declined 0.9% in the nine months ended November 2, 2024, driven by a decline in customer traffic in our retail stores. &#160;Athletics and casual continue to be our top-selling categories, while sales in the fashion categories, including boots, were weaker. &#160;We remain focused on maximizing the vertical opportunity between the Famous Footwear and Brand Portfolio segments, with Dr. Scholl&#8217;s, LifeStride, Naturalizer and Blowfish Malibu representing four of Famous Footwear&#8217;s top 20 best-selling footwear brands for the nine months ended November 2, 2024. &#160;During the first nine months of 2024, we opened 12 stores and closed 21 stores. &#160;During the nine months ended November 2, 2024, we also converted 11 stores to the new FLAIR (Famous Localized and Immersive Retail) concept, which has been successful in driving sales growth, and ended the quarter with a total of 32 FLAIR stores. &#160; &#160;</p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">30</p></div></div>
<div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:91.06%;border:0;margin:30pt 4.47% 30pt 4.47%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:4.47%;padding-right:4.47%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a style="color:#000000;font-family:&quot;'Times New Roman','Times','serif'&quot;;font-size:10pt;" href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-left:-10.0pt;margin-right:-10.0pt;max-width:100%;position:relative;width:calc(100% + 20.0pt);"><div style="padding-left:10pt;padding-right:10pt;position:relative;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Gross Profit</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Gross profit decreased&#160;$15.0 million, or 7.5%, to&#160;$183.8 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$198.8 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, our gross profit decreased to&#160;42.9% for the third quarter of 2024, from&#160;44.2% for the third quarter of 2023 as a result of higher levels of promotional activity. Higher levels of clearance selling, due in part to aged boot inventory, also negatively impacted our gross profit margin during the quarter. &#160;In addition, we experienced higher freight costs, due in part to the higher mix of e-commerce sales. &#160; &#160; &#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Gross profit decreased&#160;$15.2 million, or 2.8%, to&#160;$534.2 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$549.4 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023, driven by lower net sales. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, our gross profit decreased to&#160;44.6% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;45.3% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023, driven by higher levels of promotional activity and clearance sales. &#160; &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Selling and Administrative Expenses</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;$3.0 million, or 2.0%, to&#160;$154.0 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$151.0 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;The increase was primarily driven by higher facilities costs, including depreciation expense associated with the investments in the FLAIR store concept, and higher salary and benefits expenses. &#160;As a percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased to 36.0% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 33.6% for the third quarter of 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;$9.4 million, or 2.1%, to&#160;$453.2 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$443.8 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The increase was driven by higher facilities costs and higher salary and benefits expenses, partially offset by lower marketing expenses. &#160;As a percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased to 37.9% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 36.6% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Restructuring and Other Special Charges, Net</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Restructuring and other special charges of $0.2 million for the three and nine months ended November 2, 2024 were associated with restructuring costs, primarily severance. &#160;Restructuring and other special charges of $1.2 million and $1.3 million for the three and nine months ended October 28, 2023, respectively, were associated with expense reduction initiatives. &#160;Refer to Note 5 to the condensed consolidated financial statements for additional information related to these charges. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Operating Earnings&#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Operating earnings decreased $17.0 million to&#160;$29.6 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to $46.6 million for the third quarter of 2023, primarily reflecting the factors described above. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, operating earnings declined to 6.9%&#160;for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 10.4%&#160;for the third quarter of 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Operating earnings decreased $23.5 million to&#160;$80.8 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $104.3 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, operating earnings were 6.7%&#160;for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 8.6%&#160;for the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">31</p></div></div>

id="_Hlk135833459"></a><a id="_Hlk112353854"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Net sales of $322.9 million in the third quarter of 2024 increased $2.1&#160;million, or 0.7%, compared to the third quarter of 2023.  During the third quarter of 2024, we continued to see strong demand for new products, with momentum in fashion sneakers and certain casual footwear categories, including slingbacks, Mary Janes and ballet flats. &#160;We also had sales growth in our wide-shaft and tall boot categories, while our short boot category experienced soft demand. &#160;Our brands with premium positioning generally outperformed our other brands in the quarter. &#160;During the third quarter of 2024, we opened one store in the United States, resulting in a total of 62&#160;stores, consistent with the third quarter of 2023. &#160;In addition, we continued to expand our retail store presence in East Asia in the third quarter of 2024 by opening six new Sam Edelman stores and one new Naturalizer store. &#160;During the third quarter of 2024, we closed one Naturalizer store, resulting in a total of 49&#160;stores at the end of the third quarter of 2024, compared to 34 stores at the end of the third quarter of 2023. &#160;There were also 113 international branded stores owned and operated by third parties through franchise agreements at November 2, 2024, compared to 97 international branded stores at October 28, 2023. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Net sales decreased $21.6 million, or 2.3%, to $925.6 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $947.2 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The sales decline was driven by lower wholesale sales, partially offset by solid growth in the e-commerce business. &#160;Our net sales were unfavorably impacted by operational disruptions related to the launch of our new cloud-based ERP system in the second quarter of 2024, primarily while our e-commerce and drop-ship platforms were either offline or ramping up after the launch. As we progressed through the second quarter, the development of several key operational reports was delayed, resulting in a lack of visibility to certain data and tools we rely on to manage the wholesale business. &#160;The decrease in net sales also reflects softer demand associated with the challenging macroeconomic environment and competitive retail landscape. &#160; &#160; &#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">32</p></div></div>

1.1%, to $246.6 million at November 2, 2024, compared to $243.9 million at October 28, 2023. &#160;</span><span style="font-weight:normal;"> </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New 0pt;">Gross profit increased $1.4 million, or 1.0%, to $141.6 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to $140.2 million for the third quarter of 2023, driven by higher net sales. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, our gross profit increased slightly to&#160;43.8% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;43.7% for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Gross profit increased $3.2&#160;million, or 0.8%, to&#160;$411.3 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$408.1 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, our gross profit increased to&#160;44.4% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;43.1% for the nine months ended October 28, 2023 reflecting higher merchandise margins and a higher mix of retail sales, including e-commerce sales from our owned brands and sales from our branded retail stores, both of which have higher gross margins than our wholesale sales. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Selling and Administrative Expenses</p><a id="_Hlk112353976"></a><a id="_Hlk175151280"></a><a id="_Hlk112354002"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;$5.3 million, or 5.3%,&#160;to&#160;$106.4 million for the third quarter of 2024, compared to&#160;$101.1 million for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;The increase was primarily due to higher marketing expenses, higher salary and benefits expense and higher distribution expenses. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;to&#160;33.0% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 31.5%&#160;for the third quarter of 2023.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;$12.4 million, or 4.1%,&#160;to&#160;$311.1 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to&#160;$298.7 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023. &#160;The increase was primarily due to higher salary and benefits expense, higher marketing expenses for certain brands, including Sam Edelman and Vionic, and higher distribution expenses. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, selling and administrative expenses increased&#160;to&#160;33.6% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 31.5%&#160;for the nine months ended October 28, 2023, reflecting deleveraging of expenses over lower net sales.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Restructuring and Other Special Charges, Net</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Restructuring and other special charges of $1.1 million for the three and nine months ended November 2, 2024 were associated with restructuring costs, primarily severance. &#160;Restructuring and other special charges of $0.9 million and $1.7 million for the three and nine months ended October 28, 2023, respectively, were associated with expense reduction initiatives. &#160;Refer to Note 5 to the condensed consolidated financial statements for additional information related to these charges. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt;">Operating Earnings</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Operating earnings decreased to $34.1 million for the third quarter of 2024, from $38.2 million for the third quarter of 2023, as a result of the factors described above. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, operating earnings were 10.5% for the third quarter of 2024, compared to 11.9%&#160;for the third quarter of 2023. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Operating earnings decreased to $99.1 million for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to $107.7 million for the nine months ended October 28, 2023, as a result of the factors described above. &#160;As a&#160;percentage of net sales, operating earnings were 10.7% for the nine months ended November 2, 2024, compared to 11.4%&#160;in the nine months ended October 28, 2023.</p><a id="_d0a7f4ce_b1b8_4e7f_8986_8359050ea783"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">ELIMINATIONS AND OTHER</p><table further discussed in Note&#160;10 to the condensed consolidated financial statements, the Company maintains a revolving credit facility for working capital needs that matures on October 5, 2026. The aggregate amount available under the revolving credit facility&#160;is up to $500.0 million, subject to borrowing base restrictions,&#160;and may be increased by up to $250.0 million. &#160;Interest on the borrowings is at variable rates based on the SOFR, or the prime rate (as defined in the Credit Agreement), plus a spread.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Total debt obligations of $238.5&#160;million at November 2, 2024 increased&#160;$16.5 million, from&#160;$222.0 million at October 28, 2023, and&#160;$56.5 million, from&#160;$182.0 million at February 3, 2024. &#160;During the third quarter of 2024, we used our revolving credit facility to repurchase $50.0 million of shares of our common stock under our share repurchase program. &#160;Net interest expense for the&#160;third quarter of 2024 decreased $1.6&#160;million to $2.9&#160;million, compared to $4.5 million for the third quarter of 2023, reflecting lower average borrowings and a lower weighted-average interest rate on our revolving credit facility. &#160; &#160; &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">At November 2, 2024, we had $238.5 million in borrowings and $9.4 million in letters of forms and is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, as appropriate to allow timely objectives of the control system are met. &#160;Furthermore, the design of a control system must reflect the fact there are resource constraints, and the benefits of </p></div></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><span must be considered relative to their costs. &#160;Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, have been detected. &#160;These inherent limitations include the realities that judgments in decision-making can be faulty, and breakdowns can occur because of simple error or mistake. &#160;Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people, or by management override of the controls. &#160;The design of any system of controls is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions; over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. &#160;Because of the inherent limitations in a cost-effective control system, misstatements due to errors or fraud may occur and not be detected. &#160;Our disclosure controls and procedures are designed to provide a reasonable level of assurance that their objectives are achieved. &#160;As of November 2, 2024, management of the Company, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule&#160;13a-15(e)&#160;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934). &#160;Based upon and as of the date of
